hero.title: Chemical Engineering (UG) in Mauritius
hero.subtitle: In Mauritius, a Bachelor’s in Chemical Engineering is an undergraduate degree program for students who want to pursue a career in industrial production, chemical processes, materials, energy, pharmaceuticals, food processing and environmental technologies. **A Bachelor’s in Chemical Engineering in Mauritius for Indian Students** is an option for students interested in applying scientific and engineering principles to industrial processes.

overview: The University of Mauritius is offering a full-time Bachelor of Engineering (Honours) in Chemical Engineering, program code E404, for the 2026-2027 academic year, which is a four-year program. The program is based on the application of chemistry, mathematics, physics and engineering principles to the conversion of raw materials into useful products on an industrial scale. Students planning to **Study Chemical Engineering in Mauritius** can explore this undergraduate option with guidance from **Edu-Hawk Worldwide**.

faq.question: What are the eligibility criteria for Indian students?
faq.answer: Most applicants need to have Class 12 or an equivalent recognized qualification with relevant mathematics and science subjects. The exact combination of subjects and minimum grades will depend on the applicant’s educational board and should be confirmed with the university. Students should verify Chemical Engineering Eligibility in Mauritius before applying.

faq.question: How much does it cost to study Chemical Engineering in Mauritius in INR?
faq.answer: For the relevant intake, please contact the University of Mauritius directly to confirm tuition fees. The indicative living expenses vary from ₹4.67 lakh to ₹8.89 lakh per annum excluding tuition and one time expenses. The final budget will be decided by the university fee schedule and the lifestyle of the student.

faq.question: What are the job opportunities after Chemical Engineering?
faq.answer: Graduates can pursue careers in process engineering, chemical production, manufacturing, quality control, environmental engineering, water treatment, food processing and research and development. What the employer wants, combined with your technical skills and the practical experience you can show, will be what your job prospects are like.
